definition: A promise stands for a value that is not available yet. It later becomes fulfilled with a value or rejected with a failure, and other code can attach work to run at that moment. Some languages call the same idea a future, and a few split the producer side from a read-only handle.
details: A promise settles once. Attaching a callback after it has settled still runs the callback with the stored result.
examples: The result of an HTTP request that has not finished
A file read that will either return bytes or fail
